solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Army officer no longer having faith fell down

parts.note: Col is the standard abbreviation for colonel
a lapsed believer has stopped practising their religion

explanation.surface: A soldier of rank who has lost his religion collapses on the parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall down suddenly, so the past tense matches 'fell down'.

clue.text: Man in vehicle, one learning to drive

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle
L is the learner, from the L-plate a British learner driver displays

explanation.surface: A man sits in a car next to someone having driving lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are red-on-white L signs British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl is a man's first name, and crosswords often define any male name as 'man'.

clue.text: Aquatic creature hit hard, animal killed by another

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash someone
prey is a creature hunted and killed by a predator

explanation.surface: A water creature strikes hard, and one animal is killed by another in the food chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like jawless fish living in rivers and seas.

clue.text: Device making holes everybody heard

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: everybody means all

explanation.surface: A noisy drilling tool that the whole street can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small pointed tool for piercing leather or wood.

clue.text: Writer in bed in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the bed within the letters for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East, abbreviated SE
a crib is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: An author lies in bed in a commuter county near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties bordering London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, originally a copyist of manuscripts.

clue.text: Rejection upset boy — is young lady hiding?

indicators.note: hiding means the reversed boy holds the next letters concealed within him
upset in a down clue means the word for the boy is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Miss is the title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl turns down a distressed boy and ducks out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the boy reads DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is a rejection, a sending away or refusal of someone.

clue.text: Mother very angry rolling round

indicators.note: rolling round says the word for furious is turned to read backwards

parts.note: mad means furious

explanation.surface: An enraged mum is turning around to confront someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse or dog.

clue.text: Emotional episode when doctor meets an old woman

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, an 'old woman' in slang

explanation.surface: A tearful scene occurs when a GP visits an elderly patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a dramatic, emotionally charged situation or incident.

clue.text: Important times exciting most men

indicators.note: exciting suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Big occasions are those that thrill most men.
explanation.definitionFit: Moments can be significant points in time, as in 'moments of history'.

clue.text: Walker who keeps talking incoherently?

definitions.meaning: a hiker who strolls in the countryside for pleasure
one who speaks at length in a confused, wandering way

explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is both a country hiker and someone who rambles on in talk.

clue.text: Son getting somewhat hot in crowd

parts.note: warm is moderately hot

explanation.surface: A boy gets rather overheated in a packed throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large dense mass of people or insects.

clue.text: Nation a bit angrier possibly? Time to probe that

indicators.note: to probe means to go into, so the letter is pushed inside the rearranged letters
possibly says the letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Is this country getting a little more irate? Time to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A BIT ANGRIER; 'to probe' puts T within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The island of England, Scotland and Wales forms a country of the United Kingdom, commonly called a nation.

clue.text: Sees cast in action, having taken on board right performers

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the deeds word
having taken on board says the deeds word also holds the letter for right

parts.note: acts are actions or deeds

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sees a cast in action at the theatre, with the right players on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the theatre company but signals the anagram, making ESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Actresses are female actors, people who perform on stage or screen.

clue.text: Canine mammal you spotted without tail entering animal shelter

indicators.note: entering means the shortened word goes into the shelter word

parts.note: a cote is a small shelter for doves or sheep

indicators.note: without tail means the clue word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: You spot a wild dog creeping into a farm shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' is only surface padding; 'without tail' docks the clue's own word to YO.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a wild North American member of the dog family.

clue.text: Conservative idiot is hanging around university, a plotter

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: hanging around means the small word surrounds the letter for university

explanation.surface: A Tory fool loiters near a campus, scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius led the conspiracy to assassinate Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassius was one of the chief conspirators against Caesar, famously so in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Seaman meets girl, a god

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman
Iris is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sailor meets a young woman who turns out to be divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian deity of the underworld and the afterlife.

clue.text: Unusual coin found in food

parts.note: rare means uncommon
a bit was an old British coin, as in the threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A collectable coin turns up in someone's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The threepenny bit was a small pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rarebit, is a dish of melted cheese on toast.

clue.text: Georgia, university revolutionary lacking social graces

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A student radical from a Georgia campus is socially awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche describes someone clumsy and tactless in company.

clue.text: Well, senators could be such obstructive people!

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians in a legislature are exactly the sort who block progress.
explanation.walkthrough: In politics stonewalling is delaying business by obstruction, like a filibuster.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewallers block or delay by refusing to cooperate or answer.

clue.text: Group of monks giving command

definitions.meaning: a religious community living under one rule, like the Benedictines

explanation.definitionFit: An order is both a monastic brotherhood and an authoritative instruction.

clue.text: Try Bach's final piece on organ

indicators.note: final piece means the closing letter of the composer's name

parts.note: the ear is the organ of ...

explanation.surface: Have a go at playing a Bach composition on a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt', but it is the legal sense: a judge tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who tries a case listens to it in court, so to try is to hear.

clue.text: Home established finally by American river

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: An American has finally set up home by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river of Pakistan, giving India its name.

clue.text: Competent old man tethered by rope

indicators.note: tethered by means the father word is held inside the rope word

parts.note: a cable is a thick rope
pa is father, informally 'the old man'

explanation.surface: A skilled elderly man is tied up with a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means able and efficient, having the skill to do something.

clue.text: Grass from peak, looking up

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a top is a summit

explanation.surface: Turf seen from a mountain summit as one gazes skyward.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot and grass are both slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Knight maybe is returning with king

indicators.note: returning says the little word is read backwards

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A knight perhaps comes back accompanied by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title given to a knight, so a knight is one example.

clue.text: Publication one found at sports event

definitions.meaning: a British weekly political magazine of that name
someone watching a match from the stands

explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names the British weekly, and a member of the crowd watches the game.
